title: A blind test at 137 E: the unchanged North Pacific ventilation model gave the sigma0 26.5 AOU gain and its pre-1988 fall; across nine sites it is too large in the west, too small in the east
abstract: Question: campaign work explained the North Pacific oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 by the loss of its late-winter outcrop, and a tracer-calibrated ventilation model (sci:4525c37f) gave the AOU gains at 25-46 N and at Station ALOHA, all on the eastern and southern gyre limbs. Does the unchanged model predict the western return limb, and is its known eastern deficit a sensitivity error or a regional process? Approach: we wrote tests first, ran the model unchanged (8 tracer-calibrated sets, 3 configurations) and hashed its predictions for the Japan Meteorological Agency 137 E section (20-30 N) before we read any oxygen value west of 140 E. Then we computed AOU, salinity and nutrients on density surfaces from World Ocean Database bottle data (1965-2022). Results: AOU on 26.5 rose by 8.8 umol/kg (95% interval 6.3-10.6) from 1988-1996 to 2009-2025; the model gave 8.2-22.8 (median 12.4; depth-dependent oxygen use 4.2-8.7), so the size test passed (ratio 0.71). The annual series follows the model (r 0.54-0.70, all runs). Without a fit, the model also gave lower AOU in 1988-1996 than in 1967-1984 (observed -4.3, -6.7 to -2.1; model -18.6 to +6.0). 2009-2025 AOU is the highest of any 17-yr window since 1967. The gain is within one water type (salinity explains 20%) and regenerated (dNO3/dAOU 0.136). The pre-set onset test failed because of AOU highs in 1976-1979 and 1985-1987; after 1993 the observed rise came earlier than modelled. Added: across nine sites the observed/model ratio rises to the east (Spearman 0.70, p 0.036): 0.35-0.78 west of the dateline and at 137 E, 1.4-2.1 in the transition zone, at ALOHA and off California. 137 E is the oldest downstream site in the model, yet the model is not too small there, so the eastern excess needs an eastern process, not a larger ventilation sensitivity. Limitations: few bottle cruises after 2012 (CTD oxygen excluded by a pre-set offset rule; GLODAP fills some years and agrees); a 1984-1996 baseline gives +6.0 (ratio 0.49); 3-fold model sensitivity spread; cross-site analysis added after the tests, n 9.

citations.reason: Model code, fields and tracer calibration used unchanged; its prediction passes at 137 E and at the 1967-1984 level, but its regional errors show an east-west pattern.
Prediction and WOD-reader code and region ratios reused; this is a second blind test on the western limb, and the ALOHA excess is placed in an eastern pattern.
Observed 160 E-180 annual AOU series for the onset and lag tests.
Outcrop mechanism of the sigma0 26.5 oxygen loss; 137 E adds the western return limb.
Downstream spread of the loss after about 1990; 137 E rises after 1993.
Regenerated loss; 137 E nitrate rises at near-Redfield ratio. Its post-2008 California gap agrees with an eastern process.
Unmodelled salt gain off California, one candidate eastern process for the eastern excess.
Interannual winter forcing may explain the short 137 E AOU episodes that the decadal model misses (not tested here).
